operations.name: Stream-time aggregation (1-minute tumbling window flush)
operations.description: Flink consumes clicks, dedupes by event_id, and on each minute boundary flushes aggregates into ClickHouse exactly-once.

steps.title: Flink source consumes next click batch
steps.action: Each Flink subtask pulls from its assigned Kafka partitions. A subtask owns the aggregation state for every ad_id hashing into its partition set.

steps.title: Dedupe by event_id (idempotency key)
steps.action: Each event's event_id is looked up in RocksDB keyed-state (TTL 24h). Seen before → drop and do not count. Otherwise store and continue.
steps.decision: idempotency key already seen — drop, do not count

steps.title: KeyBy(ad_id) and update tumbling 1-min window
steps.action: Events are re-keyed by ad_id; the event-time tumbling window operator maintains per-(ad_id, minute) count + HLL. The window does not emit yet — it waits for the watermark to pass the window end.
steps.codeOrCommand: stream.keyBy(Click::adId).window(TumblingEventTimeWindows.of(Time.minutes(1))).aggregate(new AggregateFunction<Click, Accum, Row> { public Accum add(Click c, Accum a) { a.count += 1; a.hll.offer(c.userIdHash); return a; } public Row getResult(Accum a) { return Row.of(a.adId, a.bucketTs, a.count, a.hll.serialize); } });

steps.title: Watermark crosses window end — flush
steps.action: When the watermark reaches 14:33:00 + 2 min allowed-lateness, the 14:32 window closes. Flink emits one row per ad_id active in that minute and begins 2PC commit into ClickHouse.

steps.title: ClickHouse durably commits the aggregate rows
steps.action: The 2PC sink writes to a staging part; on Flink checkpoint completion, commit atomically attaches the part to the table. Either all 4120 rows are visible or none are.
steps.codeOrCommand:
-- sink-side, per-txn
INSERT INTO ad_agg_1m_staging_flink_chk_88421 (ad_id, campaign_id, bucket_ts, clicks, uniq_users_hll, source)
VALUES (?,?, '2026-04-24 14:32:00',?,?, 'stream'),...; -- on commit
ALTER TABLE ad_agg_1m ATTACH PART 'flink_chk_88421_part';

operations.title: Nightly batch correction
operations.name: Nightly batch correction
operations.description: At 02:00 UTC a Spark job re-aggregates the full prior day from S3 + DLQ with bot filtering and dedupe, and overwrites the 'stream' rows with 'batch' rows in ClickHouse.

steps.title: Spark job launches, reads raw events
steps.action: Airflow triggers the corrector. Spark reads the day's Parquet partitions plus the DLQ; total input is ~440 GB for a typical day.
steps.codeOrCommand:
val events = spark.read.parquet("s3://ad-events/date=2026-04-23/")
val dlq = spark.read.parquet("s3://ad-dlq/date=2026-04-23/")
val all = events.unionByName(dlq)
all.count // ~1.02B rows including late + DLQ

steps.title: S3 streams Parquet blocks to executors
steps.action: S3 returns Parquet row-groups to Spark executors in parallel. Heavy but well-parallelized — throughput-limited by executor count, not S3.

steps.title: Dedupe, bot-filter, re-aggregate
steps.action: Spark deduplicates by event_id (full-day window, not the stream's 24h RocksDB), applies full-context bot filtering, and re-windows to 1-minute buckets.
steps.codeOrCommand: val clean = all.dropDuplicates("event_id").transform(BotFilter.applyFullDay _) // > 50 clicks/60s same ip_trunc = bot val agg = clean.groupBy($"ad_id", $"campaign_id", window($"ts_server_ms", "1 minute").as("w")).agg( count(lit(1)).as("clicks"), approx_count_distinct($"user_id_hash").as("uniq_users") ).withColumn("bucket_ts", $"w.start").withColumn("source", lit("batch")).drop("w")

steps.title: Write batch rows, ReplacingMergeTree supersedes stream rows
steps.action: Spark writes the batch-sourced rows to ClickHouse. Because the engine is `ReplacingMergeTree(source)` and `source='batch' > source='stream'`, the next merge pass replaces streaming rows for the same (campaign_id, ad_id, bucket_ts) key.
steps.decision: batch source supersedes stream source on merge

steps.title: Report API invalidates Redis cache for T-1
steps.action: On successful batch completion, the corrector emits a signal to the Report API, which invalidates the T-1 day cache entries so advertiser queries re-read the freshly corrected data.

tradeoffs.chosen: Lambda (stream + nightly batch) rather than pure streaming
tradeoffs.rationale: True exactly-once at this volume is expensive and fragile; a cheaper stream that is overwritten by a trustworthy batch gives you both freshness and correctness, at the cost of two codebases.

tradeoffs.chosen: Event time with a bounded watermark
tradeoffs.rationale: Processing-time windows are simpler but double-count after recovery and under-count during lag spikes; event time with a 10-second watermark matches how advertisers actually think about 'clicks per minute'.

tradeoffs.chosen: Idempotency key at ingest plus idempotent upsert at the sink
tradeoffs.rationale: Kafka exactly-once across job restarts is achievable but brittle. Two cheap guards — a hashed event id and a PK-based upsert — cover every realistic replay path.

tradeoffs.chosen: Columnar OLAP (ClickHouse/Pinot) over a row-oriented OLTP database
tradeoffs.rationale: Advertiser queries are wide scans over time ranges with group-bys on ad_id and campaign_id; columnar storage with compression is 10-100x faster for those shapes and cheaper to store.

tradeoffs.chosen: Archive every event to cold storage for at least 30 days
tradeoffs.rationale: The batch corrector, compliance audits, and ML training pipelines all require the raw log. Kafka retention is too short and too expensive to serve that role directly.
Hot ads concentrate traffic, but aggregation is per-ad so co-locating events per partition keeps state local to a single Flink task and avoids cross-partition shuffles.
